summary:
The clearest signal on the board today is the MIL consensus against ATL — all four ratings stack MIL with deltas from +1.83 to +2.13, and MIL as a picked team is hitting 63% (26-15, n=41) with a strong-play mark of 65% and +5.0u. Bullpen is the category to trust behind that number: it's the one rating x category cell running hot across the board right now, with R1, R2, and R3 all posting 101-87 (54%) over the last 14 days, well above their season marks of 51%. BOS as the second-strongest consensus play (all four ratings clustered +0.92 to +1.26) fits the same profile — BOS picks are 76% (29-9, n=38) on the year and 76% strong-play with +15.0u, arguably the safest team-trust angle on the slate. TBR is a name to watch even where the model is split: TBR ranks as a top strong-play team (78%, +22.0u) but today's TBR@BAL card actually splits, with R1/R2 leaning BAL and R3/R4 flipping to TBR — that disagreement is a fade signal given TBR's road strength and Freddy Peralta on the mound, so don't force this one into an auto-strong slot.

Trends remains the most reliable category anchor — 54% over the last 14 (102-86, n=188) with trends+runs the best combo at 56.2% (241-188, n=429) — and it agrees with the rest of the model on every one of today's non-split games, which is a good filter: PHI over STL, CHC fading in SEA, ARI over CIN, LAD over PIT, CHW over NYM, and KCR over DET are all clean trends+bullpen consensus spots. Steer clear of SP-driven confidence today; SP is the coldest category leaguewide at 46% over 14 days for R1-R3, and several of the split games (SDP/MIN, TOR/NYY, ATH/HOU) hinge on unsettled or TBD starters, which is exactly where that softness bites hardest. R1's overall strong-play window is also cold right now (44-48, -2.0u last 14), so lean R2 and R3 for tie-breaks — both show positive 14-day unit trends (+3.0u each) and R3 carries the best 30-day and season P/L of the group (+27.0u, +42.0u).
